cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stand with me at the club meeting. We're going to save the garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Absolutely. Who's trying to build on it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We are. Our extension plan puts the kitchen there. I'll withdraw my signature first; you follow me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So we're opposing the plan we persuaded everyone to support?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You can explain why we sold it to them, and I'll explain what we missed. Are you beside me for that, or shall I leave room for you on the other side?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits garden ally; A3 reveals their own plan as threat and sets withdrawal order; A5 assigns public accountability roles and asks which side B will stand on.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 builder question with their signed kitchen plan; A5 uses B4 prior persuasion to divide the explanations owed.

relationship.evidence: B2 eagerly supports garden then B4 recognizes the reversal and its reputational cost, meaningful participation.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 recognition of past persuasion into a personally costly second recruitment.

specificity.evidence: A1 club garden meeting and A3 proposed kitchen explain the physical conflict without outside history.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 longer binary choice is clear and character-led; other side is rhetorical pressure, not a new literal seating rule.
